problem_statement: Our cache bounds memory two ways at once: an entry lives at most `ttl` seconds from when it was set, and the cache holds at most `cap` entries, evicting the least-recently-used when full. Today neither is quite right: get returns an entry however stale it is, and when the cache is full it evicts the oldest-inserted key — not the least-recently-used — so a hot entry that was set first gets evicted while a cold one set later survives. get must return None for an expired entry (and drop it), a get must refresh the entry's recency, an expired entry never occupies capacity — a set drops expired entries before evicting by recency — and eviction must remove the live entry whose last use is oldest. A set on an existing key refreshes both its value and its expiry.
